items.title: An Anthropic AI model sent a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police
items.summary: Anthropic did not discover this behavior until over two months after its AI submitted the false tip.

items.title: Amazon and others are done keeping data center deals secret. Is it enough to build trust?
items.summary: Amazon says it will stop using NDAs when negotiating data center deals with local governments, following a similar move from Microsoft earlier this year. items.title: Danu Robotics’ fight to build a better recycling robot
items.summary: For six years, Danu founder Amy Ma has been working on a better way to sort recyclable waste.

items.title: We can’t help treating AI like it’s human. But should we?
items.summary: "When we are drawn into even the most primitive exchanges with a relational artifact, we believe it cares for us," Dr. Sherry Turkle writes. "And we are wired to care for it in return."

items.title: a16z’s Olivia Moore on the state of consumer AI
items.summary: Moore sees a huge opportunity in consumer AI, particularly if the industry can tap into revenue streams beyond just subscriptions and API charges.

items.title: Pretend you’re sitting at Elizabeth Holmes’ desk on this weirdly detailed website
items.summary: With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents from the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to rifle through the Theranos founder's desk.

items.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims, warn of chilling effect
items.summary: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute allegations of mishandling sensitive information, warning in an open letter that their dismissals are creating a chilling effect on the company’s AI safety culture.

items.title: Ben Affleck is an AI nerd, and the internet is impressed
items.summary: Ben Affleck is going viral for his deep knowledge of AI, from neural networks and transformers to open weights. The actor, who sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix earlier this year, is proving he's more than just a Hollywood star.

items.title: Popular AI leaderboard Arena nearly doubles valuation to $3.1B valuation in 10 months
items.summary: The company behind the popular LMArena leaderboard has raised $200 million led by Lightspeed and Khosla, and is now measuring AI models on alignment issues such as lying.

items.title: OpenAI’s revenue is reportedly $20 billion less than previously projected
items.summary: It had previously been reported that the AI lab's annualized revenue was some $70 billion, but a new report claims it's a whole lot less than that.

items.title: Google brings agentic AI to Gemini, starting with businesses
items.summary: Google is turning Gemini into an AI agent that can plan, execute tasks, and work across business apps and systems. The agent can delegate work to subagents, use multiple AI models, and even gets its own workplace identity, complete with an email address.

items.title: Anthropic changes usage policy to ban model abuse and election interference
items.summary: Anthropic's updated usage policy explicitly prohibits users from repeatedly abusing Claude in extreme cases, though ordinary frustration and criticism are still allowed. The new rules also address election interference, deceptive campaigns, weapons software, and surveillance.

items.title: OpenAI’s math solutions aren’t meeting the field’s standards yet
items.summary: OpenAI's flood of proofs deviated from the guidelines set by a group of mathematical researchers consulted by the frontier lab.

items.title: Natura’s $99 smart ring puts AI agents on your finger
items.summary: Natura’s $99 Interface smart ring lets you summon AI agents with the press of a finger to complete tasks, capture thoughts, and control devices — while doubling as a health tracker.

items.title: Goodfire says its new ‘inside-out’ monitors catch rogue AI agents at a fraction of the cost
items.summary: Goodfire just launched what it says is a cheaper way to keep AI agents in check: Instead of paying a second AI to read everything an agent does, its monitors peek inside the model while it works and only call in backup when something looks fishy.
